archetype.name: Gunslinger (accurate)
archetype.definition: Maye earns most of his value attacking 10-plus yards downfield with real accuracy, and accepts a higher interception rate as the price of throwing into those windows, with scrambling as his escape when the pocket breaks down.

report.headline: Still a top-15 passer living downfield, but the picks and an ankle injury cloud everything
report.take:
Maye arrived at 2026 off a 2025 that ranked third in EPA per play, CPOE and yards per attempt. This year he has been good rather than great. His 0.146 EPA per dropback ranks 14th of 54 and his 6.81 CPOE ranks 4th. Against the league average he is still well ahead, by 1.62 yards per attempt and 8 points of CPOE. The drop from last year shows up in two places: completion rate is down 6.4 points, and interceptions run 0.63 a game higher. His 11 picks rank 52nd of 54.

The passing game runs on the vertical throws. Attempts of 10-plus air yards have added 45.8 EPA, while everything under 10 has added just 12.9. Throws behind the line have cost 23.9 EPA by themselves, at a 23.9% success rate. The deep ball is the best part of his game: 0.661 EPA per attempt, a 17.5 CPOE and 8 touchdowns on 40 throws. That aggressiveness also produces most of the turnovers, with 9 of the 11 interceptions on 10-plus attempts. Direction tells a similar story. Throws to the right have produced 12 TDs and 0.40 EPA per play. Throws to the left are below zero, with 7 interceptions. That gap is sharp enough to look like a read or footwork habit rather than noise, though 119 attempts is a moderate sample.

The raw numbers undersell the middle of his season and oversell how clean it was. Weeks 1 through 3 were rough, with negative passing EPA in all three. The Weeks 4 through 8 run looked like 2025 again, highlighted by 374 yards and 25.4 EPA against the Raiders and a 15.3 CPOE in Chicago. Across his last five games he sits at 0.20 EPA per dropback and 8.73 adjusted net yards per dropback. His 3-INT game against Green Bay was played under heavy pressure, with a 24.2% bad-throw rate. In Week 10 he played 17% of snaps before the ankle injury, which drags down the last-three numbers. He is holding the ball longer this year (up 0.19 seconds) while choosing tight windows less often (aggressiveness down 6.1 points). Even so, his pressure-to-sack rate of 26.3% is a real improvement on the 40.5% and 35.6% of his first two years.

The immediate issue is availability. He is listed Doubtful with an ankle injury. Vrabel said he wouldn't expect him back coming out of the Week 11 bye, and the line he would be throwing behind is missing its center and Walter Rouse. When he returns, expect an efficient downfield passer who still throws too many interceptions. The talent level suggests the completion rate rebounds somewhat. The interception rate is part of how he plays, and is likely to stay above average.

strengths.title: Downfield accuracy drives the offense
strengths.body: His deep throws produce 0.661 EPA per attempt and a 17.5 CPOE, and passes of 10-plus air yards account for most of his passing value. He was a top-3 CPOE passer last year, so this is a lasting skill rather than a hot streak. The touchdown rate on deep balls will cool some, but the efficiency should hold.

strengths.title: Scrambles rescue broken plays
strengths.body: Twenty-seven scrambles have gained 221 yards and 17 first downs at 0.637 EPA apiece. That pays back a lot of the sacks that come with his longer time to throw. Designed runs, by contrast, have been poor, at 2.1 yards per carry. His legs work as an escape hatch, not as a run-game feature, and the ankle threatens exactly that.

strengths.title: Middle-of-season form was real
strengths.body: Over Weeks 6 through 10 his EPA per dropback was 0.20 and his adjusted net yards per dropback 8.73, both well above his full-season marks. Several of those games came against good defenses, including Chicago and Green Bay. It looked like his 2025 level returning before the injury.

concerns.title: Ankle injury, likely out Week 12
concerns.body: He is Doubtful, and the coach said he wouldn't expect him back after the bye. The listed return date is only an estimate. An ankle injury also threatens the scrambling and off-platform play his efficiency leans on.

concerns.title: Interceptions are the cost of attacking
concerns.body: His 4.0% interception rate ranks 45th of 54, and he is already past last year's interception total in seven fewer games. Most of the picks come on intermediate and deep throws, and seven have come to the left side. Some of that is a price worth paying for his downfield EPA, but the left-side split points to a correctable flaw.

concerns.title: Weak spots: screens, third down, red zone
concerns.body: Throws behind the line have cost 23.9 EPA, and he has been below zero on both third down and in the red zone. Seven of his third-down dropbacks ended in sacks. The screens reflect play design and blocking more than Maye himself. With the center and Rouse out, the third-down pressure problem may get worse before it gets better.

trend.note: He started cold with three negative-EPA games, then ran hot from Week 4 through Week 8. Green Bay's pressure produced three picks, and the Week 10 ankle injury ended his day after 17% of snaps. His form had been trending up before the injury.

nextGame.headline: Probably won't play; if he does, Chargers' deep defense invites shots
nextGame.body:
If Maye plays, the matchup suits him. The Chargers allow 0.853 EPA on deep passes, 30th in the league, which is exactly where he does his damage. They are stingy underneath, allowing -0.013 EPA on short throws (10th). They also rarely finish sacks (26th in sack rate) despite a top-10 hit rate, a profile his scrambling can exploit. Their offense ranks last in EPA and has the most run-heavy pass rate over expected in the league, so expect a short, low-possession game that caps his volume. Their WR1 and TE1 numbers suggest Douglas and Henry face tougher work than a deep shot would.

Availability decides this game. Maye is Doubtful, and Vrabel all but ruled him out of the first game back from the bye. A.J. Brown is questionable with a hamstring after limping post-game, and center Ben Brown and lineman Walter Rouse are out. That is a weakened front even if Maye somehow suits up. On the Chargers' side, defensive tackle Eboigbe and depth defensive backs Waxter and Williamson were inactive, a modest help in the trenches and secondary.

keyMatchups.title: His deep ball vs leaky deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: His best throw meets one of the league's worst deep defenses. If he plays even at reduced mobility, the downfield shots are the path to a big game.

keyMatchups.title: Short game runs into resistance
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers clamp down on short throws, and Maye's screens and quick game already struggle. Expect fewer easy completions and more reliance on intermediate-to-deep windows.

keyMatchups.title: Slow script limits volume
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers run far more than expected and have the league's worst offense by EPA. Possessions should be scarce, which works against a big passing-yardage total.

nextGame.watch: Whether Maye practices at all during the bye week; anything short of full participation means he likely sits.

restOfSeason.body:
Assuming he returns within a game or two, the base case is a passer around his season form: roughly 210 to 260 passing yards and 1.4 to 2.0 touchdowns a game, driven by a deep game that has held up across two seasons. His completion rate should drift back toward his talent level, given a CPOE that ranked 3rd last year and ranks 4th now. The interception rate is the part to bet against fixing itself. It comes with how he attacks, and 0.6 to 1.0 picks a game is a reasonable range.

The ankle is the main swing factor. Scrambling has been an important source of value for him, so expect fewer rushing yards (roughly 10 to 25 a game) and possibly more sacks until he is fully mobile. That matters more behind an offensive line missing its center and Rouse. A healthy A.J. Brown would add an outside receiver to a target tree led by Douglas and Henry. The Patriots' defense ranks 24th and allows explosive passes at a high rate, so shootout scripts should keep his volume up when he plays.
swingFactors: Ankle recovery timeline and mobility on return
Health of the center and A.J. Brown
Cleaning up throws to the left side

confidence.note: His skill level is clear, but an ankle injury with no diagnosis and an uncertain return makes near-term outcomes hard to predict.
